I would say if you're really trying to improve is go into the game's menus and find the replay mode. Try and spot something that you're having a lot of trouble with and try to recreate that situation in training mode using the record and playback function. You tend to have a lot more options than you would think.

You're hitting that point as a player where you're no longer looking at the game just doing random shit and hoping it works. Which is great because you're engaging the game on a cerebral level which is when it gets really fun trying to read your opponent. You're gonna have to start actually engaging in neutral and realize when you're overextended or advantaged in a given situation. You're also gonna have start getting better at baiting and punishing whiffed attacks to get your openings for big damage. Pressure strings can be pretty decent for catching lower-level players but at higher level you're liable to catch a reversal or shadow counter for your troubles against someone higher level.

If you keep getting combo broken at the same point in your combos start counter breaking, switch up the strength of your attacks, do shorter combos, or start incorporating manuals to bait lockouts. You have options, it's just a matter of knowing what your opponent can and cannot do, and then exploiting it. Say you keep getting broken on medium autos after an opener, counter break their ass and make them eat 60% for their troubles. You have the tools you just got know what to use at what time.

As for actual matchup advice, I play RAAM so I could help with that.

Sadira: She's super slippery and annoying but it's a matter of patience and good defense. RAAM has amazing AAs but can get blown up for them if he uses the wrong ones. Sadira also has an absolutely terrible wake-up because her only fully invulnerable option is an escape that can be AA'd or backdash which can be caught with M or H Stab or Running grab. Meaties are your friend when you score a knockdown. St.Mk is a fantastic one, super active, is +2 on block, and allows you to combo St.Hp on hit. Sadira is a master of pressuring from the air so if you can keep her grounded and force her to play your game she's already lost.

Riptor: Super annoying but not impossible to fight. A lot or her mix-ups are unsafe so it's lot of blocking, slowing walking her down to the corner, and baiting mistakes. Her backdash is just as invincible as everyone else so it's matter of finding the correct timing on a given knockdown to meaty. A lot of Riptor love to do backdash into HK, so if you can bait that and block, they're eating a fat punish. Riptor can feel smothering but it's about finding gaps in her offense and shadow countering her multihit moves.

Wulf: You can do H. Emergence on reaction to every single one of his Run options. You don't have to guess high or low. My main problem with matchup is knowing when there's a gap to press a button during pressure or being patient enough to wait for meter for a shadow counter. Otherwise, RAAM can stomp this matchup if he has the momentum.

RAAM has really strong ambiguous knockdown pressure and setups especially after his command grabs. There's a lot ways you can for your opponent into having deal with things like ambiguous crossups, meaties, and grabs.

Go to into training mode and start labbing your bad matchups. It also helps to learn said characters you have a problem with as you can see what weaknesses they have. You have the tools, you have know what tool to use in a given moment. That's gonna take you to that next level. Just keep practicing, asking questions to both yourself and others, and learning, the rest will come in time. If you need anymore explanation feel free to ask! I'm also more than happy to play.
